What the official sources say

  • Appeals from board of equalization rulings fixing value must be taken within 30 calendar days of the notice under 40-3-21, with notice filed with the board secretary and circuit court clerk plus bond. (Ala. Code 40-3-25; source)
  • Either party may demand a jury trial by written demand within 10 days after the appeal is taken. (Ala. Code 40-3-25; source)
  • If the board has not ruled by November 30, the taxpayer has 30 calendar days from the final decision to pay taxes without penalty or appeal to circuit court. (Ala. Code 40-3-25; source)
  • A taxpayer appealing must pay taxes at the prior-year assessment or post a supersedeas bond, or the appeal is dismissed; circuit court cannot enjoin collection. (Ala. Code 40-3-25; source)
  • Appeal from circuit court judgment goes directly to the Alabama Supreme Court within 42 days of entry of judgment. (Ala. Code 40-3-25; source)
  • Assessment ratios: Class I utilities 30%; Class II all property not otherwise classified 20%; Class III agricultural, forest and residential property 10% of market value. (Ala. Code 40-8-1; source)

Who assesses and collects property tax in Alabama?

Property tax in Alabama is local work with state oversight. The Department of Revenue's Property Tax Division sets standards and procedures for equalization of values, while the assessing itself happens at the county courthouse. The department says all taxable real and personal property, except public utility property, is assessed locally by the county assessing official.

Its FAQ adds that all property tax other than public utility tax is assessed and collected through the 67 county tax offices. If you have a question about a parcel, the county office is the place to ask. The state division can be reached at 334-242-1525 and is based at 375 South Ripley Street in Montgomery.

Because the work is split this way, the same state rules produce different bills from one county to the next. Millage rates are set locally, a point the department's own examples make clear.

When are Alabama property taxes due, and when do they become delinquent?

The department says property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Its division page explains that the lien date is October 1 and that taxes become due the following October 1.

The department also publishes a short calendar for what happens to unpaid accounts:

MonthStep
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to the probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

One easy mistake is to wait for a bill. The Revenue Commissioner is not required to mail tax notices and does so only as a courtesy, so you owe the tax whether or not a statement arrives.

How is the amount of tax worked out?

Alabama multiplies an assessed value by a millage rate. The department explains that a mill is one-tenth of one cent, and the number of mills a taxing agency charges is applied to the assessed value of the property.

The department gives a worked example: a $100,000 appraised value at a 10 percent assessment rate gives a $10,000 assessed value. At a county millage rate of .0325, the tax comes to $325. The example is an illustration of the formula, not a prediction for your house, since millage differs by county and by taxing district.

A seller who wants to estimate the buyer's tax should ask the county office for the assessed value and total millage on the parcel rather than apply a rule of thumb.

How often are Alabama properties revalued?

Every Alabama county operates under annual equalization, and the assessing official must review one quarter of the county each year. A full review of all property in a county is finished over a four-year cycle.

The department says the goal is to even out assessments between similar and dissimilar properties and to produce small yearly increases in market value rather than a large jump at the end of a four-year cycle. It also names two reasons a bill goes up: a millage increase, which needs a vote of the citizens or action by the taxing authority such as the County Commission, and an increase in appraised value from a court-ordered reappraisal or from economic gains in the county.

For a seller, that means a bill can rise without any work on the house, and a buyer's first bill may differ from yours.

Do you have to report improvements to the house?

Yes. Owners or their agents must visit the Revenue Commissioner's office no later than December 31 to sign a new assessment reporting improvements made or structures removed on or before October 1 of that year.

  • New structures or additions
  • Swimming pools
  • Extensive repairs, remodeling or renovations
  • A new fireplace, extra bathroom, patio, deck, carport or garage

Normal maintenance does not trigger a new assessment, and the department gives re-roofing, minor repairs and painting as examples. Sellers who finished a project shortly before listing should check that it was reported.

How do you appeal an Alabama property tax valuation?

If you think your value is wrong, you may file a written protest with the County Board of Equalization. The department says owners have 30 days to file an appeal after receiving written notice of valuation, and it points to Code sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25 for the process.

  • Start with the county assessing official, who can explain how the value was set.
  • File the written protest inside the 30-day window.
  • Gather proof such as recent repair estimates, photos of damage, or sale prices of similar houses.
  • Ask the county office whether any payment is due while the protest is pending.

Appeals that go beyond the board follow the court procedure in section 40-3-25, so ask the county office or an Alabama attorney about the next step if the board denies your protest.

Which owners get relief?

The department says owners 65 or older, owners who are permanently and totally disabled regardless of age, and blind owners are exempt from the state portion of property tax. County taxes may still be due. The owner claims the homestead exemption at the local taxing official's office.

The exemption turns on occupancy as a primary residence, which means investors and out-of-town heirs usually do not qualify. Our Alabama homestead exemption guide lays out the types in detail.

Manufactured home owners over 65 are exempt from the registration fee on an owner-occupied manufactured home, though they pay the $5 issuance fee.

What taxes and fees come up when you sell?

Beyond the yearly bill, a sale triggers a recording tax. Under section 40-22-1, the privilege or license tax on a deed is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500, with the base set by the actual purchase price. The tax applies only to the value above a mortgage or vendor's lien that already paid mortgage tax.

  • The deed must be accompanied by proof of the actual purchase price, using a form from the Department of Revenue.
  • The judge of probate calculates the tax and collects it before recording the deed.
  • Two thirds of the tax goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury.
  • Intentional failure to give requested proof, or false proof, carries a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater.

How the year's property tax is divided between seller and buyer is set by the contract, so read that section of your closing paperwork closely.

What can you do if you are behind on Alabama property tax?

Pay as soon as you can, because the timetable moves quickly after December 31. Once an account goes to the probate court in February, the road to a May tax sale is short. If a home carries back taxes alongside other problems, such as repairs, an inherited title or a tenant, selling may be easier than catching up.

A cash sale can resolve the tax from the proceeds at closing, and we buy houses as-is across Alabama with no repairs needed. You can request an offer and decide later whether it makes sense.

More questions about Alabama Property Tax Guide

When are property taxes due in Alabama?

Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31, according to the Department of Revenue. The lien date is October 1.

Who do I contact about my Alabama property tax bill?

Your county tax office. The state says all property tax other than public utility tax is assessed and collected through the 67 county offices.

How long do I have to appeal my valuation?

You have 30 days after receiving written notice of valuation to file a written protest with the County Board of Equalization.

Do I still owe tax if I never got a bill?

Yes. The Revenue Commissioner mails notices only as a courtesy, so the tax is owed whether or not a statement arrives.

How is Alabama property tax calculated?

The assessed value is multiplied by the millage rate. In the department's example, a $100,000 appraised value at a 10 percent assessment rate and a .0325 county millage rate comes to $325.

Do I have to report improvements to my house?

Yes, owners must report improvements or removals made on or before October 1 by signing a new assessment at the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31. Normal maintenance such as painting or re-roofing does not require one.

title: Alabama Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home
content:
Alabama Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Homestead Exemption sale
  • Turn the Alabama Homestead Exemption offer down and you owe us nothing

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Under age 65: exemption up to $4,000 assessed value (H-1: $4,000 state and $2,000 county assessed value). (Homestead Exemptions | Alabama Department of Revenue; source)
  • Apply at the local county office. (Homestead Exemptions | Alabama Department of Revenue; source)
Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What counts as a homestead for Alabama property tax?

For tax purposes, the Alabama Department of Revenue defines a homestead as a single-family, owner-occupied dwelling and the land that goes with it, up to 160 acres. The owner has to live there as a primary residence on the first day of the tax year for which the exemption is requested.

That wording matters for anyone planning a sale. A house that sits empty after a move, a rental, or a home held by heirs who live elsewhere does not fit the plain description. A house the owner lives in does, and the owner may qualify for a reduction in assessed value or, for some older and disabled owners, a larger break.

The department publishes its homestead page and points owners to the Code of Alabama, Title 40, sections 9-19 through 9-21, for the legal text. It also posts yearly memoranda that explain the federal and state income tests used for the income-limited types.

Which homestead types does Alabama list, and who gets each one?

Alabama sorts homestead relief into four named types, labeled H-1 through H-4, set out under Act 2013-295. Age, income and disability decide which one applies to a given owner.

TypeWho it is forWhat the department says it does
H-1Owners under 65 who are not disabled$4,000 of assessed value on the state portion and $2,000 of assessed value on the county portion
H-2Owners 65 or older with adjusted gross income under $12,000 on the latest state return, or owners retired because of permanent and total disabilityExempt from the state portion, plus $5,000 of assessed value on the county portion, school district tax included
H-3 (age 65+)Owners 65 or older with net taxable income of $12,000 or less on the combined federal returnExempt from all ad valorem taxes
H-3 (disabled)Owners who are permanently and totally disabledExempt from all ad valorem taxes, with no income limit
H-4Owners 65 or older with income above $12,000 on the latest Alabama returnExempt from the state portion and given the regular $2,000 assessed-value exemption on county taxes

Notice that the figures are assessed values, not market values. Because Alabama assesses residential property at a fraction of market value, an exemption of a few thousand dollars of assessed value removes a much larger slice of the house price from the tax base.

How do the state, county and school pieces of the bill differ?

Alabama homestead relief is applied separately to the state, county and school district parts of the bill, which is why two neighbors of different ages can see very different results.

The department's tables show the pattern. Owners who are not 65 receive up to $4,000 of assessed value off the state tax, and no income limit applies. Owners 65 or older, owners with a permanent and total disability, and blind owners have no maximum assessed value on the state exemption, again with no income limit and the same 160-acre ceiling.

The county side is more varied. The department notes that counties, municipalities or other taxing authorities may grant a homestead exemption of up to $4,000 in assessed value, and that county school tax is collected on some categories and not on others. The result is a patchwork that depends on the county and on the owner. A seller who wants to know what a buyer will pay should call the local assessing office rather than assume the statewide minimum.

Where do you apply for the Alabama homestead exemption?

You apply at your local county office, not with the state. The Department of Revenue says plainly to visit the county office where the home sits, and its FAQ repeats that all property tax other than public utility property is assessed and collected through the 67 county tax offices.

  • Expect to show that you own the house and live in it as your primary residence.
  • If you are claiming the age-based types, expect to show your age and, where the type has an income limit, the tax return the department's memorandum names.
  • If you are claiming disability, the department posts a physician's affidavit that a doctor uses to verify permanent and total disability.
  • Ask the office which type it has on file for you.

The department lists county office contacts on its site, and the Property Tax Division can be reached at 334-242-1525 if you cannot tell which office handles your parcel.

What does the principal residence exemption add?

Alabama also has a combined state, county and city principal residence exemption under Title 40, section 9-21. It covers two groups: owners 65 or older with income of no more than $12,000 on the combined federal return, and owners who are permanently and totally disabled regardless of age.

For both groups the department lists no maximum assessed value, a land limit of 160 acres, and no collection of county school tax. The disabled category has no income limit. The relief closely matches what the H-3 type describes.

What happens to the exemption when you sell the house?

The department's page does not say what happens to an exemption in the middle of a year when ownership changes, so a seller should not guess. The only rule the page states is the occupancy test: the owner must live in the home as a primary residence on the first day of the tax year.

That test points to a practical split. If you owned and lived in the house on that date, the exemption question for that year turned on your occupancy, and a buyer who moves in later starts the process with the county office. A buyer who plans to rent the house or flip it will not meet the occupancy test, so an investor should price the property at the tax level without an exemption.

  • Ask the county office how a sale date affects your current-year bill.
  • Check the payoff or title company statement for how property tax is split between seller and buyer.
  • Keep your copy of the exemption approval in case the title company asks for it.

What if you inherited a house and are thinking about selling?

An heir who does not live in the inherited house does not meet the department's occupancy wording, so the decedent's exemption should not be assumed to continue. If the previous owner was 65 or older and paid little or no tax, the first bill after the death can look much higher.

Plan for that. Taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the department, and the County Revenue Commissioner is not required to mail tax notices. A bill that goes unpaid during a slow estate can turn into a larger problem, so check the account with the county as early as you can.

Heirs who want to skip repairs, carrying costs and uncertainty sometimes choose to sell as-is. A cash buyer can close on your timeline and handle the cleanup, which is one way to stop the tax clock running against you. You can compare options at your own pace, and you owe nothing if you decline an offer.

Which dates should a seller track each year?

Four dates drive most homestead and tax decisions in Alabama: October 1, December 31, January 1 and the date you list or sign a contract. The department publishes a short timetable for the tax cycle.

WhenWhat happens
October 1Taxes are due
January 1Taxes are delinquent
FebruaryDelinquent accounts go to the probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilProperty is advertised for sale
MayTax sale

A homestead exemption lowers the amount owed but does not move any of these dates.

Are manufactured homes handled differently?

Yes, in one respect. The department says owners of manufactured homes who are over 65 are exempt from the registration fee on an owner-occupied manufactured home, but they still pay the $5 issuance fee.

That is separate from the homestead types above, and it matters if you are selling a mobile or manufactured home on land you own. Ask the county office which fees and exemptions apply to the home itself and which apply to the land, since the two can be billed differently.

More questions about Alabama Homestead Exemption

Who qualifies for the Alabama homestead exemption?

An owner of a single-family home who lives in it as a primary residence on the first day of the tax year, on up to 160 acres. The amount depends on age, income and disability status, and the department lists types H-1 through H-4.

Is there an age requirement for the largest exemption?

The biggest breaks go to owners 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled owners, and in some state categories blind owners. The H-3 type for people 65 or older also has an income limit of $12,000 on the combined federal return, while the disabled H-3 type has no income limit.

How much is the basic exemption for owners under 65?

The department lists $4,000 of assessed value on the state portion and $2,000 of assessed value on the county portion for H-1 owners. Counties and other taxing authorities may grant up to $4,000 of assessed value on their own.

Do I apply with the state or the county?

You apply at your county office. The Department of Revenue publishes the rules, but county offices assess and collect the tax.

When are Alabama property taxes due?

The department says property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. The County Revenue Commissioner does not have to mail a bill, so you owe the tax whether or not a statement arrives.

Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?

The department's page does not address a mid-year sale. A buyer must apply at the county office, and the occupancy test looks at who lives in the home on the first day of the tax year.

title: Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling
content:
Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax: What Heirs Owe When Selling

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax sale
  • Turn the Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Alabama House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax is established by Title 40, Chapter 15. (Alabama Fiduciary, Estate, and Inheritance Tax | ALDOR; source)
  • Estates of decedents dying after December 31, 2004 are not required to file with Alabama. (Alabama Fiduciary, Estate, and Inheritance Tax | ALDOR; source)
Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Alabama have an estate tax or inheritance tax?

No. The Alabama Department of Revenue states that estates of people who die after December 31, 2004 are not required to file an Alabama estate tax return. The state still has Chapter 15 of Title 40 in its code, titled Estate and Inheritance Tax, so the statute is on the books even though the filing requirement has lapsed.

The reason is how the old tax worked. Alabama's filing requirement was tied to the credit that federal estate tax law once allowed for state death taxes. Federal legislation passed in 2001 phased that credit out, and the revenue department says the result is that no state filing is due for deaths after 2004.

For anyone who inherits a house in Alabama, that means no state death tax bill stands between the heirs and a sale. The county property tax, the deed recording step and any income tax the estate owes still matter.

What does the Alabama Department of Revenue say about trusts and estates?

The department's trusts and estates page covers the income tax that estates and trusts pay, which is a separate matter from any death tax. That page also repeats the point that deaths after 2004 do not trigger an Alabama estate tax filing.

An estate that earns income after the owner dies, for example from rent on the house or interest on a bank account, may have to file a fiduciary income tax return. The key rules:

  • Alabama Form 41 is the Fiduciary Income Tax Return, and the filing duty comes from Section 40-18-29(a) of the Alabama Code.
  • All resident trusts with net income over $1,500 for the year must file.
  • All non-resident trusts with any Alabama-derived net income after deductions must file.
  • A trust that claims a qualifying net operating loss must file in the year of the loss to carry that credit into later years.
  • Grantor trusts have their own filing rules under Sections 40-18-25(g) and 40-18-29.

Executors should read the Form 41 instructions for the estate's own facts.

When is the fiduciary income tax return due, and can it be extended?

The Alabama fiduciary return is due on the same date as the matching federal return. If that date lands on a Saturday, Sunday or state holiday, the due date moves to the next business day.

Trusts and estates get an automatic extension to file that follows the extension on the federal return. The matching federal extension form has to be sent in with the Alabama return. The department is clear that more time to file is not more time to pay, so the tax owed is still due by the original date.

Two e-filing triggers are also listed on the page:

  • Estates or trusts with 20 or more beneficiaries at the end of the taxable year must e-file their Alabama fiduciary returns for that year and every later year.
  • A tax preparer who prepares 25 or more acceptable original fiduciary returns with software in a calendar year must e-file all of that preparer's fiduciary returns from then on.

The executor answers to the department for any income the estate earns.

What is the Alabama estate tax waiver, and do you still need one?

The Estate Tax Waiver is a form, listed as Form EST-1, that the Department of Revenue still shows among its most popular fiduciary forms.

The Alabama Code now offers a simpler route. Section 40-15-13 lets the personal representative of an estate sign and record an affidavit in the county of the decedent's last domicile, and in any county where the probate estate is pending. The affidavit says either that the estate is not taxable, or that it is taxable and the right copy of a federal estate tax return has been or will be filed with the department on time.

The affidavit must open by stating it is filed under that section and must contain:

  • The decedent's legal name and Social Security number.
  • The decedent's legal residence, including county, and the date of death.
  • Whether a federal estate tax return will be filed.
  • The name and address of the administrator or executor.

Once the affidavit is recorded, people who hold or manage estate assets may transfer them in reliance on it without getting a waiver, unless they know or should know that it is wrong.

Can the state still have a lien on an inherited Alabama house?

Yes, in principle. Section 40-15-13(a) gives the State of Alabama a lien for any tax and interest that is or may become due under the estate tax chapter on all property the decedent died owning, in whatever form it now takes and on any property acquired in its place.

In practice, because estates of people who died after 2004 have no filing requirement, there is usually nothing for that lien to secure. It can still show up in the paperwork on an older estate or on a title search of a house whose owner died long ago.

Before listing, an heir can check:

  • Find the date of death. After December 31, 2004 means no Alabama estate tax return is required.
  • Ask the probate court whether an affidavit under Section 40-15-13 is already on record.
  • Keep the recorded affidavit in the closing file.

What does Title 40, Chapter 15 contain?

Chapter 15 is the Alabama code's estate and inheritance tax chapter, and its section titles show how the tax was designed. Justia's copy of the 2025 Code lists the sections below, with a few gaps in the numbering where sections were removed.

SectionSubject
40-15-1Meaning of executor, administrator or legal representative
40-15-2Amount of tax
40-15-3Duplicate of federal return filed by executor; computation by the department
40-15-4Time of payment and filing return; extension of time
40-15-13Lien of state; affidavit by personal representative
40-15-18State and federal estate taxes paid out of estate property

The executor filed a duplicate of the federal return and the department computed the state amount from it.

What taxes does an heir still face when selling an inherited house in Alabama?

Three Alabama items remain even with no estate tax: the property tax bill, the recordation tax on the deed, and income tax questions for the estate. Each has its own office and timing.

Property tax follows a statewide calendar published by the Department of Revenue:

MonthStep
October 1Taxes due
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

A house that sits through an estate administration can slip past the January 1 delinquency date if nobody pays the October bill. Heirs who are weighing a quick sale often want that bill current before a closing date is set.

The deed that moves the house to a buyer is taxed on recording. Section 40-22-1 of the Alabama Code sets the privilege or license tax at 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or part of $500. Only the value above any mortgage that has already paid mortgage tax is taxed. Two thirds of the tax goes to the state treasury and one third to the county treasury.

What happens at the probate judge's office when a deed is recorded?

The judge of probate in the county where the house sits collects the recordation tax and the recording fee, then records the deed. Section 40-22-1 requires that the tax be paid before the instrument is received for record.

The same section adds details that matter to a seller:

  • A deed or similar instrument must come with proof of the actual purchase price. If the property was not sold, proof of actual value is needed.
  • The Department of Revenue developed a form for attesting to the price or value, and a person who uses it in good faith does not need other documentation.
  • If no proof is given, the judge of probate bases the tax on the most recent assessment and may add a penalty.
  • The penalty for deliberately withholding requested proof, or giving false proof, is $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater.
  • Deeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect title are among the exemptions, and the judge of probate stamps them "No Tax Collected."
  • A problem with the price proof does not undo the recording or the notice that recording gives.

Heirs who deed a house out of a trust or estate should ask the probate office which category their instrument falls into before they show up with a check.

How does an as-is cash sale fit with an estate?

A cash buyer can purchase an inherited Alabama house as it stands, which spares the heirs from making repairs or cleaning out the property before closing. Heirs should still confirm who has authority to sign, since the personal representative usually handles that when the house is in probate.

Because Alabama no longer requires an estate tax return for deaths after 2004, the closing checklist is shorter than in states that still collect a death tax. Typical items are the recorded affidavit or letters from the probate court, a current property tax receipt, payoff letters for any mortgage, and the recordation tax paid on the deed.

If you have inherited a house, our team can talk through timing with you.

More questions about Alabama Estate and Inheritance Tax

Does Alabama charge an inheritance tax on heirs?

No. The Alabama Department of Revenue says estates of decedents dying after December 31, 2004 are not required to file with Alabama, and its page describes no separate tax on heirs.

Do I need an Alabama estate tax waiver to sell an inherited house?

Usually not for deaths after 2004. Section 40-15-13 lets the personal representative record an affidavit that the estate is not taxable, and people holding estate assets may rely on it unless they know it is wrong. A title company can say what it wants to see.

Does an estate file an Alabama income tax return?

It may. The department's fiduciary page says Form 41 is required of resident trusts with net income over $1,500 and of non-resident trusts with any Alabama net income. An executor should check the form instructions for the estate's facts.

How much is Alabama's deed recordation tax?

Section 40-22-1 sets it at 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed or fraction of $500, reduced by value covered by mortgages that already paid mortgage tax. Proof of the purchase price must accompany the deed.

When do Alabama property taxes become delinquent?

The Department of Revenue timetable shows taxes due October 1 and delinquent January 1. Unpaid taxes are turned over to the probate court in February and can be advertised in April and sold in May.

What the official sources say

  • Appeal from district court eviction judgment to circuit court within seven days of entry. (Ala. Code 35-9A-461(d); source)
  • Tenant appeal does not stop a writ of possession unless the tenant pays rent into court as it comes due. (Ala. Code 35-9A-461(d); source)
  • After judgment for landlord, writ of possession issues on application with a seven-day automatic stay. (Ala. Code 35-9A-461(e); source)
  • If personal service fails, service may be by delivery to an occupant or posting on the door plus first-class mailing. (Ala. Code 35-9A-461; source)

Which court handles an eviction in Alabama?

Either the district court or the circuit court, depending on their established jurisdictions, and the case belongs in the county where the rented property sits. Section 35-9A-461(b) of the Alabama Code says eviction actions get precedence in scheduling over all other civil cases.

The landlord's lawsuit follows the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure and the Alabama Rules of Appellate Procedure, except where the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act changes them. In plain terms, an Alabama eviction is a regular civil case that has been put on a faster track.

For an owner of a rented house, the county line matters. A house in Madison County is heard in Madison County, and a house in Mobile County is heard in Mobile County, even if the landlord lives somewhere else.

What are the steps of an Alabama eviction from notice to writ?

The usual path runs from a written termination notice, to a lawsuit, to a judgment, to a writ of possession. The statute does not give a single calendar for the whole thing, so the days below come only from the sections cited.

StepWhat the Code saysSection
Termination notice, unpaid rentLease ends if rent and late fees are not paid within seven business days after receipt35-9A-421(b)
Termination notice, other breachTermination date not less than seven business days after receipt, unless cured35-9A-421(a)
Lawsuit filedDistrict or circuit court in the property county, with scheduling precedence35-9A-461(b)
Appeal windowSeven days after entry of the district court eviction judgment35-9A-461(d)
Writ of possessionIssues on the landlord's application, after a seven day automatic stay35-9A-461(e)

The notice periods run in business days, so weekends and holidays stretch them.

How does a tenant get served with an eviction lawsuit in Alabama?

Service follows the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure, with a special fallback written into the landlord and tenant statute. If a sheriff, constable or process server cannot reach the defendant in person, Section 35-9A-461(c) allows two alternatives.

  • Delivering the notice to any person who is sui juris, meaning legally able to act, and lives on the premises.
  • If after reasonable effort no one is found living there, posting a copy on the door of the premises.
  • A mailing step follows the posting: on the day of posting or by the close of the next business day, the notice of filing must be sent by first class mail to the premises' mailing address, or to the defendant's last known address if the premises has none.
  • Service by posting is complete as of the date of mailing.

The statute also directs that an entry of the posting and mailing be made on the return filed in the case.

How long does a tenant have to appeal an Alabama eviction judgment?

Seven days after the entry of judgment. Any party can appeal an eviction judgment entered by a district court to the circuit court within that window, and the statute sets this deadline notwithstanding the general appeal rule in Section 12-12-70(a).

A timely post-judgment motion under the civil rules suspends the clock. The full appeal time then runs from the date the order on that motion is entered, or from the date the motion is denied by operation of law under Rule 59.1.

When either side appeals, the clerk schedules the case for trial as a preferred case and it is to be set within 60 days of the filing of the appeal.

Does a tenant's appeal stop the eviction in Alabama?

Only if the tenant pays rent into court. Section 35-9A-461(d) says a tenant's appeal to circuit court or to an appellate court does not prevent a writ of restitution or possession unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk all rent properly payable under the lease since the date the action was filed.

The tenant must then keep paying each rent installment to the clerk as it comes due while the appeal is pending. If there is a dispute about the amount, the court decides what is properly payable.

  • If the tenant misses a payment, the court on motion shall issue the writ and the landlord is placed in full possession.
  • When the appeal ends, the court tells the clerk what to do with the money paid in.
  • If the landlord took possession and the judgment is later reversed, the circuit court may issue a writ to restore the tenant, but not as against a third party.

What happens after the judge rules for the landlord?

A writ of possession issues when the landlord applies for it, and the statute adds a seven day automatic stay on that writ. Section 35-9A-461(e) says that seven day period applies notwithstanding Rule 62 of the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure.

If a tenant removed under the writ re-enters the home without just cause, the tenant can be held in contempt, and successive writs may issue as needed to carry out the judgment. The Code does not, in the section cited here, set out who carries out the removal or how many days the tenant gets to pack.

Anyone planning a sale around a tenant's departure should treat the seven day stay and a possible appeal as the first two moving parts, then ask the court clerk or an attorney what the local practice is for the writ.

What other Alabama rules can change how an eviction plays out?

Four sections of the landlord and tenant act tend to come up. Each one is short enough to summarize, and each can be checked on the legislature's or Justia's copy of the Code.

  • Holdover (35-9A-441(c)): a tenant who stays after the term or termination without consent can be sued for possession. If the holdover is willful and not in good faith, the landlord may also recover up to three months' periodic rent or actual damages, whichever is greater, plus reasonable attorney fees.
  • Month-to-month notice (35-9A-441(b)): either side may end a month-to-month tenancy by written notice at least 30 days before the periodic rental date named in the notice.
  • Retaliation (35-9A-501): a landlord may not raise rent, cut services or bring an action for possession because the tenant complained to a code agency, complained about maintenance, or joined a tenants' group. The landlord can still sue for possession when the tenant is in default on rent, or for other material lease violations.
  • Security deposits (35-9A-201): money held as security may be applied to accrued rent and damages, with an itemized written notice and any balance delivered 60 days after the tenancy ends and possession is delivered.

Section 35-9A-201 also caps most deposits at one month's periodic rent, with exceptions for pets, changes to the premises and increased liability risks.

Can I sell a rented house in Alabama while an eviction is pending?

Owners do it, and the practical question is whether the buyer will take the house with the tenant or the court case still open. Some buyers want the home empty first. We can look at an as-is house with the process still under way.

Before agreeing to anything, an owner should know four facts: whether a termination notice has been delivered, whether a suit has been filed, whether a judgment has been entered, and whether any appeal money has been paid into the circuit court. Those four answers tell a buyer how much time and risk remain.

We buy houses as they stand, including rentals with tenant problems. Tell our team where your case is, and we can talk about timing without asking you to fix, clean or list the house first.

More questions about Alabama Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House

Which court hears an eviction case in Alabama?

The district court or the circuit court, based on their jurisdiction, in the county where the property is. Section 35-9A-461(b) gives eviction actions precedence over other civil cases in scheduling.

How many days does a tenant have to appeal an Alabama eviction?

Seven days after the district court enters the eviction judgment. A timely post-judgment motion suspends that period until the court rules on it.

Does an appeal keep the tenant in the house?

Not by itself. The appeal does not prevent a writ of possession unless the tenant pays the circuit court clerk the rent due since the filing date and keeps paying rent as it comes due.

What is the automatic stay on a writ of possession?

After a judgment for the landlord and an application for the writ, Section 35-9A-461(e) sets the automatic stay at seven days, replacing the general stay in Rule 62.

How is a tenant served if the sheriff cannot find them?

The papers may be delivered to a person living on the premises, or posted on the door if no one is found, followed by first class mail the same day or by the close of the next business day.

How fast must an appealed eviction be tried?

The clerk schedules it as a preferred case and it is to be set for trial within 60 days of the filing of the appeal, according to Section 35-9A-461(d).

title: Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property
content:
Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property

Cash Home Buyers in Alabama
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property sale

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Summary distribution of a small estate is started by verified petition in the probate court of the county of the decedent's domicile; no bond required. (Ala. Code 43-2-692; source)
  • Distribution may proceed once 30 days have passed since publication of notice and 30 days since Alabama Medicaid Agency received notice. (Ala. Code 43-2-692; source)
  • Small estate means an estate not exceeding the 'small estate amount' (defined in 43-2-691(7)); 2025 HB164 amended these sections. (Ala. Code 43-2-691; source)
Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How is probate organized under the Alabama Code?

Alabama administers decedents' estates under Title 43 of the Code of Alabama, and Chapter 2 of that title, called Administration of Estates, is the main procedural map. It breaks the work into twenty articles that follow the order of a typical estate.

ArticleTopic
2Grant of letters testamentary or of administration
3Notice of appointment of executors or administrators
4Bonds of executors and administrators
13Collection, inventory and appraisement of personal property
15Claims and debts
17Renting and sale of real estate
18Settlements and distributions
19Insolvent estates
20Probate Procedure Act

For anyone trying to sell an inherited house, article 17 and the Probate Procedure Act in article 20 matter most, because they deal with how real estate can be rented or sold.

Who has the legal right to sell an inherited house in Alabama?

The authority usually belongs to the personal representative the probate court appoints, called an executor when a will names one and an administrator when there is no will. A buyer's title company will want to see that appointment before it relies on anyone's signature.

Section 43-2-843 lists what a personal representative may properly do, unless the will or a court order says otherwise. Several items bear on a house sale: retaining assets pending distribution, performing the decedent's contracts to convey land, paying taxes and other administration expenses, insuring the assets, hiring appraisers and attorneys, and leasing property for a term not exceeding one year.

The same section says that when the decedent had an enforceable contract to convey land, the representative may deliver a deed for cash, or deliver a deed in escrow so the proceeds go to the decedent's successors when paid. That is the kind of paperwork a buyer's title company will want to see.

What is the order of inheritance when there is no will?

Alabama's intestacy rules decide who inherits when no valid will exists. Section 43-8-42 sets the order for everything that does not pass to a surviving spouse, or for the whole estate if there is no spouse.

  • To the decedent's issue, taking equally if they are of the same degree of kinship, or by representation if not.
  • If there are no issue, to the decedent's parent or parents equally.
  • If there are no issue or parents, to the issue of the parents or either of them by representation.
  • If none of those survive, to grandparents and their issue, with half of the estate going to the paternal side and half to the maternal side.

This order explains why an inherited house often has several owners. When children inherit equally, every one of them has a stake in the sale, and the personal representative needs a clear path to the buyer.

Why does an Alabama probate sale take time?

A house cannot be sold until someone has authority to sign for the estate, and that authority comes from the probate court. The Code gives letters, notice of appointment, bonds and the inventory of personal property their own articles, and each of those steps can slow things down when records are scattered or relatives disagree. The same section also lets a representative insure estate assets, borrow or advance money to protect the estate, and keep idle estate cash in federally insured interest-bearing accounts.

Claims against the estate also have to be handled. Article 15 covers claims and debts, article 19 addresses insolvent estates, and article 18 governs settlements and distributions. A representative who sells the house before sorting out debts may face questions from heirs or creditors later.

Property taxes keep running in the meantime. Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and the personal representative's list of permitted acts includes paying taxes and assessments incident to administration.

What does a deed from an estate cost to record?

When a deed is recorded, Alabama collects a privilege or license tax under section 40-22-1: 50 cents for each $500 of value, or fraction of $500, for instruments conveying property worth more than $500. The tax applies to the value above any mortgage or vendor's lien on which mortgage tax was already paid.

  • The deed must come with proof of the actual purchase price, or the actual value if the property was not sold, on a form the Department of Revenue provides.
  • The judge of probate calculates the tax when the deed is presented.
  • If no proof is given, the tax is based on the most recent assessment, and a penalty may apply.
  • The penalty for intentionally withholding proof after a specific request, or for false proof, is $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater.

The statute exempts deeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect a title, among other items, so the exact treatment of an estate transfer is worth confirming with the county probate office.

Where do probate and property records live?

In Alabama the judge of probate in each county serves as the recording office for deeds, which is why the county probate court shows up in both an estate matter and a real estate closing. The same office that opens an estate file is the office that records the deed to a buyer.

A seller can save time by gathering these before a buyer's closing agent asks, and the probate office can say which of them it needs for your estate:

  • A certified copy of the letters showing who has authority to sign.
  • The recorded deed or other record that put the decedent on title.
  • The most recent property tax bill and payment record.
  • A list of heirs, with contact information, if there was no will.

When does selling the house as-is make sense for an estate?

An as-is sale makes sense when the estate does not have the time, money or energy to repair and market the house. Probate already involves court steps, creditor questions and family decisions, so a house that needs a roof, cleaning or a full rehab adds to the load.

A cash buyer purchases a house in its present condition, which means no repairs, no staging and no showings. The sale still has to run through the estate's authority, and a personal representative should work with the probate court and an Alabama attorney on timing, approvals and the deed. Heirs get to compare an offer against a traditional listing, and there is no obligation if they pass.

More questions about Alabama Probate Process and Selling Inherited Property

Do you always need probate to sell an inherited house in Alabama?

A house titled in the decedent's name generally needs someone with court-granted authority to sign. The Code calls that authority letters testamentary or of administration, and a title company will ask to see them. Ask the county probate office whether another route fits your estate.

Who inherits if there is no will?

Section 43-8-42 sends the estate to the decedent's issue first, then to the parents, then to the issue of the parents, then to grandparents and their issue, after any share that goes to a surviving spouse.

Can a personal representative sell real estate?

Yes, within the powers the will and court orders allow. Section 43-2-843 lists the transactions a representative may properly make, and article 17 of Chapter 2 deals with the renting and sale of real estate.

Are property taxes still due while the estate is open?

Yes. Alabama taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, and paying taxes is among the acts a personal representative may do.

What does it cost to record the deed?

Under section 40-22-1 the recordation tax is 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction of $500 on conveyances above $500, plus the probate office's recording fee. The tax is based on the actual purchase price or value.

Who records the deed in Alabama?

The judge of probate in the county where the property sits receives instruments for record and collects the recordation tax.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Upon sale or exchange of property, the entire gain or loss is recognized except as provided in the section. (Ala. Code 40-18-8(a); source)
Selling in Alabama?
We buy Alabama houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Does Alabama have a separate capital gains tax on a house sale?

Alabama taxes a gain on a house inside its regular individual income tax, and the individual rate section sets no separate capital gains rate. The tax on individuals in Ala. Code 40-18-5 is one three-step schedule, and a recognized gain is simply part of the income it applies to.

Federal tax rules on home sales are a separate subject, and we did not review them for this page. This guide sticks to what the Alabama Code and the Alabama Department of Revenue say, so confirm federal treatment with the IRS or a tax professional.

How does Alabama calculate the gain on a sale?

The gain is the amount realized minus the adjusted basis. Section 40-18-7 says gain from a sale of property is the excess of the amount realized over the adjusted basis, and a loss is the excess of basis over the amount realized.

The amount realized is the money received plus the fair and reasonable market value of anything else received. Section 40-18-8(a) then says that on a sale or exchange, the entire gain or loss is recognized unless the section provides an exception.

  • Amount realized: cash received plus the fair market value of other property received.
  • Adjusted basis: the starting figure set by Section 40-18-6, which this page does not walk through.
  • Taxes tied to the sale: under Section 40-18-15(a)(3)(h), specified taxes paid in connection with disposing of property reduce the amount realized.
  • Installment sales: Section 40-18-7(d) allows the part of each installment that represents gain to be taxed in the year the payment is received.

What Alabama tax rates apply to the gain?

Alabama taxes taxable income at 2%, 4% and 5%, depending on filing status and income. The table shows the brackets in Section 40-18-5. They apply to taxable income after deductions, so a gain is not taxed on its own.

Filing status2% on taxable income up to4% on income over that, up to5% on income over
Single, head of family, married filing separately$500$3,000$3,000
Married filing jointly$1,000$6,000$6,000

Under that schedule, every dollar of taxable income above $3,000 for a single filer, or above $6,000 for joint filers, is taxed at 5%. That describes the statute and is not a prediction of your bill. Your actual tax depends on deductions, other income and any exclusions, so run the numbers with a preparer.

Which deductions can lower the Alabama tax on a sale?

Alabama lets individuals deduct federal income tax paid and several other items. Section 40-18-15(c) allows a deduction for federal income tax paid or accrued within the taxable year, which can reduce the Alabama tax on a large gain.

Section 40-18-15 also lists other deductions that sometimes line up with a house sale or its aftermath.

  • State and local real property taxes, only to the extent they are deductible for federal purposes.
  • Interest on indebtedness, limited to what is allowable federally.
  • Casualty and theft losses on personal property, following federal rules for those losses.
  • Medical and dental expenses above 4.0 percent of adjusted gross income, instead of the federal 7.5 percent threshold.
  • Moving expenses, but only where the new principal place of work is in Alabama.
  • Up to $35,000 spent removing architectural or transportation barriers for people with certain disabilities.

The optional standard deduction is the other path. Under Section 40-18-15(b)(4), a single taxpayer with adjusted gross income under $25,500 gets $3,000, a married couple filing jointly under $25,500 gets $8,500, and each is reduced as income rises, down to $2,500 and $5,000. A big gain will usually push income well past those thresholds.

Are there ways to defer or avoid recognizing the gain?

Yes, in specific cases. Section 40-18-8 lists the exceptions to full recognition, and a few relate to real estate.

  • Like-kind exchanges: if an exchange meets 26 U.S.C. 1031, Alabama determines recognized gain under that section.
  • Involuntary conversions: if the taxpayer elects treatment under 26 U.S.C. 1033, such as after a condemnation or destruction, Alabama follows that election.
  • Transfers between spouses or former spouses: gain or loss follows 26 U.S.C. 1041.
  • Transfers to a trust: gain or loss is not recognized on the transfer of property to a trust.

Alabama does not write its own rules for these. It points back to the federal Internal Revenue Code sections, so the federal conditions control, including deadlines. A sale to a stranger at market price falls under the general rule and is recognized.

What if I live outside Alabama?

A nonresident who sells Alabama real estate faces limits on some deductions. Section 40-18-15(e) restricts several deductions to items tied to Alabama property or an Alabama business. Section 40-18-15(c) also prorates the federal income tax deduction for a nonresident by the share of adjusted gross income that comes from Alabama sources.

If you inherited a house in Alabama and live elsewhere, your preparer should check both states' rules before you file.

What is the Alabama deed tax, and who pays it?

Separate from income tax, Alabama charges a recordation privilege tax on deeds. Under Section 40-22-1, the tax is $.50 on instruments conveying property worth $500 or less, and $.50 for each $500 or fraction thereof above that.

On a $250,000 sale, that works out to 500 units and a tax of $250.00. The statute allows the taxable value to be reduced by mortgages or vendor's liens on which mortgage tax was already paid. The statute says an instrument cannot be received for record until the tax is paid.

RuleWhat Section 40-22-1 says
Rate$.50 per $500 or fraction thereof of value conveyed
Proof of priceDeed must carry proof of the actual purchase price, using the Department of Revenue form
No taxDeeds executed for nominal consideration to perfect title
Penalty$100 or 25% of tax due, whichever is greater, for failing to provide requested proof or giving false proof
SplitTwo thirds goes to the state treasury and one third to the county

When are Alabama property taxes due when I sell?

The Alabama Department of Revenue states that property taxes are due October 1 and are delinquent after December 31. If you sell part way through the year, ask your title company how the current year's bill is split, since the closing paperwork should say who pays what.

Property tax is a different subject from capital gains, but it hits the same settlement statement, and unpaid taxes can delay a closing.

How does a cash sale fit with the tax picture?

A cash sale does not change how the gain is taxed. It does change the timeline and the costs on the page: you know the sale price in advance, you avoid paying agent commissions on a listing, and the deed tax and recording still run through the probate office.

If you own an Alabama house you want to sell as is, perhaps after an inheritance, send us the address for a written cash offer. Talk to a tax professional about the gain before you sign.

More questions about Alabama Capital Gains Tax When You Sell a House

Does Alabama tax capital gains on a house sale?

Yes, as part of regular income. Under Ala. Code 40-18-8(a), the entire gain on a sale is recognized unless an exception applies, and it is taxed through the 2%, 4% and 5% brackets in Section 40-18-5.

What is Alabama's top income tax rate on a gain?

The top rate in Section 40-18-5 is 5%, which applies to taxable income over $3,000 for single filers and over $6,000 for joint filers.

Can I deduct federal income tax from my Alabama return?

Yes. Section 40-18-15(c) allows a deduction for federal income tax paid or accrued in the taxable year, and nonresidents get a proration based on Alabama-source income.

What is the Alabama deed tax rate?

It is $.50 for each $500 or fraction of value conveyed, under Section 40-22-1. The tax is collected when the deed is recorded.

When are Alabama property taxes due?

The Department of Revenue says they are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

Does a 1031 exchange work in Alabama?

Yes. Section 40-18-8(c) says that if an exchange meets the requirements of 26 U.S.C. 1031, Alabama determines the recognized gain under that section.

  • Delinquent taxpayer must be notified at least 30 days before the auction by first class mail and by newspaper (once a week for three weeks), county website, or courthouse posting. (Ala. Code 40-10-182; source)
